source_fields.uniformity: There exists a single algorithm whose guarantee holds uniformly for every admissible instance and response rule. The guarantee is not averaged over an input distribution.

description_paragraphs: $$\ell(I,\widehat{x})=F(\widehat{x})-F^\star$$
$F^\star=\inf_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}F(x)$. The existence, compactness, or initial-suboptimality assumptions ensure that the optimal value in this comparison is finite.

output.certificate: No additional certificate is required, although a method may use one internally to select its output.
description_paragraphs: Return a point $\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d$.
The output may be unqueried or constructed from the query history, provided it is feasible. No additional function value or accuracy certificate is required.
$F=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n f_i$, where the components may be nonconvex. The average $F$ is convex and has a minimizer within distance $R$ of $x_0$. Each component $f_i$ is individually $\beta$-smooth.

Unless another geometry is specified, vectors use the Euclidean norm $\|\cdot\|_2$, and matrices and higher derivatives use the corresponding operator norm. The assumptions hold uniformly throughout the declared domain.
Individual smoothness means $\|\nabla f_i(u)-\nabla f_i(v)\|_2\le\beta\|u-v\|_2$ simultaneously for every $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and every pair $u,v$ in the declared model domain.

Admissible parameter domain:

$$\begin{gathered}\varepsilon > 0,\quad d \ge 1,\quad n \ge 1,\quad \varepsilon \le \frac{\beta\,{R}^{2}}{4}\\\beta > 0,\quad R > 0\end{gathered}$$

oracle.coupling: All responses come from one fixed unknown instance. The algorithm adaptively chooses query points and any indices permitted by the interface.
description_paragraphs: Public numerical inputs: $d,\ n,\ \varepsilon,\ x_0$.
Public upper bounds: $\beta,\ R$.
The unknown objects are the component functions $f_1,\ldots,f_n$.
For each query, the algorithm chooses $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $x\in\mathbb R^d$ and receives the following information about that component.
$$\nabla f_i(x)$$
All responses come from one fixed unknown instance. The algorithm adaptively chooses query points and any indices permitted by the interface.
Find an approximate global minimizer, with accuracy measured by suboptimality of the complete objective.
$$\min_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}F(x)$$
The complete objective is the finite sum $F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)$. Component information is available only through the declared component oracle.

internal_computation_restrictions: Linear-span restriction: queries and outputs lie in the span of past gradients permitted by Definition 3.3 of the source. Randomized index selection remains allowed.
